title: How do we add two Egyptian numerals made of heels and strokes?
description: Two Egyptian numerals are added by counting each kind of symbol, then swapping every ten for one of the next symbol, smallest first. The sum is checked against ordinary numbers. Keeko's doubt is that the counts of each symbol can be left as they are.
teaching_notes: One idea: add by counting each symbol, then regroup every ten into one of the next landmark, starting from the smallest. Watch for students who stop after counting and keep fifteen of a symbol.

source: Add 8 heels and 7 strokes to 7 heels and 8 strokes in Egyptian numerals.
video_script.why: The child adds Egyptian numerals by counting each kind of symbol and regrouping ten of a symbol into one of the next, as the book does.
video_script.substitution: Count each kind of symbol together, then swap every ten for one of the next landmark, smallest first.
video_script.anchor: the book's Egyptian addition: two numerals made of heels and strokes side by side
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko stops after counting each kind and keeps fifteen of a symbol; but ten strokes make a heel and ten heels make a coil, so the counts must be regrouped
video_script.payoff_line: The sum is one coil, six heels and five strokes, which is one hundred sixty five.

final_answer.value: 1 coil, 6 heels and 5 strokes, which is 165
final_answer.spoken: one coil, six heels and five strokes, which is one hundred sixty five

hold_back: 1 coil, 6 heels and 5 strokes, which is 165
maths_rules: stroke = 1, heel = 10, coil = 100; each is 10 times the one before
15 strokes = 1 heel and 5 strokes; heels become 15 + 1 = 16
Keeko's slip: 15 heels and 15 strokes = 150 + 15 = 165 in value, but the numeral keeps ten or more of a symbol
video_script.design: One idea: count each symbol, then swap every ten, smallest first. The two numerals stay on the board while the counts and swaps appear below them.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about adding Egyptian numerals.
<bookmark mark='sym'/>A stroke is worth one, and a heel is worth ten.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must add eight heels and seven strokes to seven heels and eight strokes. How many of each symbol will the sum have?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board with the empty box

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: ten strokes slide into one heel; ten heels slide into one coil; the row stroke, heel, coil with 1, 10, 100

marks.strokes: ten strokes slide together into one heel
marks.heels: ten heels slide together into one coil
marks.plan: the words count each kind, then swap every ten appear

narration: <bookmark mark='strokes'/>Ten strokes make one heel.
<bookmark mark='heels'/>Ten heels make one coil, which is worth one hundred.
<bookmark mark='plan'/>To add, we count each kind of symbol together. Then we swap every ten for one of the next symbol.

beats.on_screen: Given: 8 heels and 7 strokes; 7 heels and 8 strokes

marks.given: the two numerals are written as 8 heels, 7 strokes and 7 heels, 8 strokes

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eight heels and seven strokes, and seven heels and eight strokes.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum in Egyptian numerals

marks.find: the words the sum are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find their sum, written in Egyptian symbols.
<bookmark mark='heels'/>Step one, count each kind of symbol together. Heels come to eight plus seven, which is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='strokes'/>Strokes come to seven plus eight, which is also fifteen.

beats.on_screen: start with strokes: 15 strokes = 1 heel and 5 strokes; heels 15 + 1 = 16

marks.swap: ten of the fifteen strokes slide into one heel, leaving five strokes

narration: <bookmark mark='swap'/>Step two, start with the smallest symbol. Ten strokes make one heel, so fifteen strokes become one heel and five strokes.
<bookmark mark='sixteen'/>The heels are now fifteen plus one, which is sixteen.

marks.swap: ten of the sixteen heels slide into one coil, leaving six heels
marks.now: the counts 1 coil, 6 heels and 5 strokes appear in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='swap'/>Step three, move up to the heels. Ten heels make one coil, so sixteen heels become one coil and six heels.
<bookmark mark='now'/>Every symbol is now used fewer than ten times, so we stop.

marks.values: the numerals are shown as 87 and 78

narration: <bookmark mark='values'/>Step four, check with ordinary numbers. Eight heels and seven strokes is eighty seven, and seven heels and eight strokes is seventy eight.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Eighty seven plus seventy eight is one hundred sixty five. Our coil, heels and strokes add to the same.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1 coil, 6 heels and 5 strokes, which is 165

marks.ans: the coil, six heels and five strokes are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum is one coil, six heels and five strokes, which is one hundred sixty five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the finished numeral
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's numeral of 15 heels and 15 strokes; ten strokes flash and slide into a heel; the crowded numeral is struck through and the answer numeral stays

marks.doubt: Keeko's numeral of fifteen heels and fifteen strokes appears
marks.flash: ten strokes flash and slide into one heel
marks.fix: the crowded numeral is struck through and the regrouped numeral stays

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is fifteen heels and fifteen strokes, because those are the counts.
<bookmark mark='flash'/>The total is right, but ten strokes are worth exactly one heel.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Egyptian numerals never keep ten of one symbol, so we must swap them, smallest first.
